accordion.description: Organizes related sections into expandable panels so readers can open the details they need.
usage: Pair each AccordionTrigger with its AccordionContent inside an AccordionItem.
Choose single or multiple expansion through the root type; use controlled values when another control must open a section.
accessibility: Use meaningful trigger text and preserve the supplied trigger and content parts for keyboard navigation and expanded-state relationships.

adjuster.description: Provides live controls for the shared motion settings and editable body profiles used across the library.
usage: Use MotionControls for a compact character, speed, and intensity panel with an optional preview.
Use Adjuster to tune body tiers, change motion categories, and import or export the shared profile as JSON.
accessibility: Keep the provided labels, numeric inputs, and status messages when composing a settings panel.
Respect the device reduced-motion preference and keep essential state changes understandable without animation.

alert.description: Displays a prominent message with context and optional actions where an issue or outcome occurs.
usage: Combine AlertTitle and AlertDescription to explain what happened and what the reader can do next.
Choose a status variant and wire AlertClose to your own dismissal state when the message can be dismissed.
accessibility: The root defaults to role="alert"; reserve that announcement priority for messages that need attention.
State the meaning in text instead of relying on the variant color or icon.

alert-dialog.description: Pauses a workflow for a focused confirmation before a consequential action proceeds.
usage: Describe the consequence with AlertDialogTitle and AlertDialogDescription, then provide explicit Action and Cancel choices.
Run the operation in the action handler and manage open state when completion depends on an asynchronous result.
accessibility: Preserve the dialog title, description, and cancel action so the focused confirmation has an accessible name and a clear exit.

aspect-ratio.description: Keeps a media container at a chosen width-to-height ratio as its available width changes.
usage: Set ratio for images, video, or previews that should retain a predictable shape.
Control the child media sizing and object-fit to decide whether it crops or leaves space.
accessibility: Provide appropriate alternative text, captions, and controls on the media itself; the ratio wrapper adds no content description.

attachment.description: Presents a file name, type, metadata, and nearby actions as a compact attachment row.
usage: Compose AttachmentType, AttachmentName, and AttachmentMeta from the file information you have.
Connect AttachmentAction handlers to your preview, download, or removal behavior.
accessibility: Give each action a clear accessible name and keep the file name readable without depending on its type icon.

avatar.description: Identifies a person or entity with an image, fallback content, or a grouped set of avatars.
usage: Place AvatarImage and AvatarFallback inside Avatar to handle image loading with initials or other fallback content.
Use AvatarGroup for a small collection and AvatarMore for a visible remaining count.
accessibility: Give meaningful images descriptive alt text; use empty alt text when adjacent text already identifies the person.
Ensure fallback initials and grouped counts have enough surrounding context to identify their meaning.

badge.description: Adds a compact status, count, or category label alongside other content.
usage: Use short text to distinguish a state or category without competing with the main content.
Add BadgeIndicator when a small visual marker helps reinforce the written status.
accessibility: Include the status meaning in text; a Badge is a span and does not supply button behavior.

breadcrumb.description: Shows the current location within a hierarchy and links back to its ancestors.
usage: Compose BreadcrumbList with linked ancestors and a final BreadcrumbPage.
Use asChild on BreadcrumbLink to integrate a router link, and wire BreadcrumbBack when a separate back action is useful.
accessibility: BreadcrumbPage marks the current page and decorative separators are hidden from assistive technology; keep ancestor link names descriptive.

bubble.description: Groups conversational content and timestamps into visually distinct message bubbles.
usage: Compose BubbleRow, BubbleContent, and BubbleTime to present a message and its timing.
Use the available bubble variants to distinguish message presentation while keeping sender information in the content.

BubbleReaction composes Button for an explicitly labelled, controlled reaction; pass aria-label and aria-pressed with your count. BubbleTyping supplies a labelled, controlled typing indicator that becomes still under quiet preferences.
The conversation surface, timestamps and speech-tail cutout use theme-aware surface/text roles in both modes. Set --bubble-surface when providing a custom surrounding surface.
accessibility: Keep messages in a meaningful reading order and include sender and time text when needed; bubble styling does not create a live region.

button.description: Triggers an action with native button behavior and an optional busy indicator.
usage: Use onClick for an action or set type="submit" when the button submits a form.
Set loading for busy feedback and disabled separately when repeat activation must be prevented.
accessibility: Give the button a clear action name, including aria-label for icon-only content.
Keep a meaningful label while loading; the busy state is exposed with aria-busy.

button-group.description: Places related actions together and can track one selected button value.
usage: Use ButtonGroupItem values with value or defaultValue to build a compact single-choice control.
Use ButtonGroupUtility and UtilityItem for adjacent actions that do not share selection state.
accessibility: Name each group with aria-label or aria-labelledby; selectable items expose their state through aria-pressed.

calendar.description: Displays a month grid for choosing a single date, with optional disabled dates and visual marks.
usage: Use selected and onSelect for a controlled date, or defaultSelected for local selection.
Pass disabled date matchers for unavailable days and required when the chosen date must remain selected.
accessibility: Preserve the calendar day and navigation parts for their keyboard and date-label behavior.
Explain the meaning of colored marks in nearby text or date labels instead of using color alone.

card.description: Groups related content, metadata, and actions into a distinct surface.
usage: Compose CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent, and CardFooter around one topic.
Choose a surface variant to establish hierarchy and put explicit links or buttons inside for actions.
accessibility: CardTitle renders an h3; fit it into the surrounding heading structure or supply the needed heading inside CardHeader. Keep interactive controls individually named.

carousel.description: Lets readers move through a horizontal collection of slides using scrolling and navigation controls.
usage: Place CarouselItem elements inside CarouselContent and add Previous, Next, or Dot controls as needed.
Use onIndexChange to synchronize a slide count or related content with the current position.
accessibility: Give the carousel region an accessible name and provide descriptive slide content.
Retain the labeled navigation buttons and the content keyboard handler when composing custom controls.

chart.description: Presents numeric comparisons as bars, lines, rings, or ranked rows with companion data-table primitives.
usage: Pass labeled data to Chart or ChartLine, or labeled segments to ChartRing.
Represent missing observations with null values and set a useful caption that describes the comparison.
accessibility: Keep the default companion data table or supply an equivalent accessible explanation if showTable is false.
Include units and labels so values can be understood without interpreting color or geometry alone.

checkbox.description: Captures an independent checked, unchecked, or indeterminate choice.
usage: The default organic selector stays close to a circle, with subtle asymmetry and cursor-responsive contour motion.
Choose organic, circle, rounded, pebble, leaf or flower; pink, blue, olive and yellow tones are available.
Use checked and onCheckedChange for controlled state or defaultChecked for a local default.
Group related options when users may choose more than one, and use indeterminate for a partially selected collection.
Use size="sm" | "default" | "lg" or a numeric16–64px size. indicator chooses auto/dot/check/diamond/flower; showIndicator={false} leaves the selected outer blob only.
accessibility: Associate each checkbox with a visible label and give a group a shared description when the choices need context.

code-block.description: Displays a code snippet with an optional caption, language label, wrapping, and copy feedback.
usage: Pass code as a string and use title or language to explain the snippet; language labels do not add syntax highlighting.
Enable wrap for long lines or use the default scrolling view, and use CopyButton when only the copy action is needed.
The copy control tries the Clipboard API and then a selection-based fallback when that API is unavailable, including on HTTP pages.
accessibility: Keep the copy status available so users hear whether copying succeeded or manual copying is needed.
Provide a descriptive caption and preserve keyboard access to overflowing code.

collapsible.description: Shows or hides one optional section without leaving the surrounding layout.
usage: Pair CollapsibleTrigger and CollapsibleContent inside a shared Collapsible root.
Use open and onOpenChange when expansion must stay in sync with application state.
accessibility: Keep the trigger keyboard-operable and use text that describes the section it expands.

combobox.description: Filters a list of options through text input and stores one selected value.
usage: Items show stable, varied blob adornments by default. Set adornment={false} to hide, supply {shape,color,icon,effect}, or pass a custom icon element.
Provide options with distinct values and readable labels for the built-in input, results, and empty state.
Use value and onValueChange to store the selection, or compose the input and item parts for custom option content.
ComboboxItem shows a persistent selected check separately from hover or keyboard emphasis. Set showIndicator=false to suppress that mark.
accessibility: Supply a specific aria-label for the input and preserve the input, list, and item parts that coordinate focus and selection.
Write a useful emptyText message when a search has no matching option.

command.description: Builds a searchable command list that users can navigate and activate from the keyboard.
usage: Items show stable, varied blob adornments by default. Set adornment={false} to hide, supply {shape,color,icon,effect}, or pass a custom icon element.
Compose CommandInput, CommandList, groups, and items, then run each command from its onSelect handler.
Use CommandDialog for a command palette and add CommandShortcut text to communicate shortcuts you implement.
accessibility: Give the command input an accessible label and include an empty-results message.
Provide a dialog title and description when using CommandDialog; shortcut text alone does not register a keyboard shortcut.

context-menu.description: Reveals contextual actions for a target through a context-menu interaction.
usage: Items show stable, varied blob adornments by default. Set adornment={false} to hide, supply {shape,color,icon,effect}, or pass a custom icon element.
Wrap the relevant target with ContextMenuTrigger and compose actions in ContextMenuContent.
Use checkbox, radio, or submenu items when the actions include stateful choices or another level.
accessibility: Keep essential actions reachable through a visible control as well as the contextual menu.
Use the supplied menu items to retain keyboard navigation and state announcements.

data-table.description: Displays records with client-side filtering, sortable columns, and paginated rows.
usage: Pass data and column definitions; provide sortValue only for columns that should sort.
Add predicate filters, set pageSize, and use page or filter callbacks when application state must track the view.
accessibility: Supply a caption and clear column headers; sortable headers expose their direction with aria-sort.
For important row actions, include clearly named controls in cells even when onRowClick is also available.

date-picker.description: Opens a calendar from a compact trigger to choose and display one date.
usage: Use date and onDateChange for controlled selection or defaultDate for a local initial date.
Pass disabled-date rules through calendarProps and formatDate to customize the displayed date.
accessibility: Use triggerProps to give the trigger a field-specific accessible name and associate any instructions with it.
Preserve the calendar and popover parts for date navigation, focus handling, and dismissal.

dialog.description: Opens a focused overlay for a task or information that needs dedicated attention.
usage: Compose a trigger, content, title, description, and close action inside Dialog.
Control open and onOpenChange when another part of the interface launches or completes the task.
accessibility: Include DialogTitle and a useful DialogDescription so the overlay has an accessible name and context.
Preserve focus handling and provide a clear close action when customizing the content.

direction.description: Sets a text direction for a subtree and shares it with direction-aware primitives.
usage: Wrap a region with dir="rtl" or dir="ltr" to match the language and layout direction.
Use a local Direction wrapper when a section needs a different direction from the rest of the page.
accessibility: Set direction to match the content and provide the appropriate lang attribute separately; direction does not identify the language.

drawer.description: Presents dialog content in a drawer surface while keeping the current page underneath.
usage: Compose DrawerTrigger, DrawerContent, title, description, and close controls for a secondary task.
Use the root open state to coordinate opening and dismissal with the surrounding interface.
Bottom travel is measured from the content and viewport, so taller content and dock gaps keep a continuous entrance and exit.
accessibility: Provide DrawerTitle and an accessible close action, and retain the dialog primitives for focus management.

dropdown-menu.description: Opens a compact menu of actions or stateful choices from a visible trigger.
usage: Items show stable, varied blob adornments by default. Set adornment={false} to hide, supply {shape,color,icon,effect}, or pass a custom icon element.
Use DropdownMenuTrigger with a named button and place related commands in the content.
Compose checkbox items, radio groups, separators, or submenus to match the action structure.
accessibility: Preserve the supplied trigger and item primitives for keyboard navigation and focus return.
Use concise item labels and expose destructive consequences in text when necessary.

dropzone.description: Collects local files through drag and drop or a native file picker and reports the selection.
usage: Handle onFilesSelected to validate selected File objects and connect your own storage or upload process.
Use multiple to limit the selection count and accept to guide the file picker; validate dropped files in the callback.
accessibility: The surface supports Enter and Space to open the picker; give it a task-specific accessible name.
Keep the selection receipt or provide equivalent status feedback that names the selected files.

empty.description: Explains an empty collection or unavailable result and creates space for a useful next step.
usage: Use EmptyTitle and EmptyDescription to distinguish a new collection from a search with no results.
Add a clear action such as creating an item or clearing a filter when that action is available.
accessibility: Use a meaningful heading and description; announce a dynamically changed result separately when the workflow requires it.

field.description: Connects a form control with its label, description, and validation message.
usage: Wrap one control in FieldControl and pair it with FieldLabel and a description or error message.
Set invalid from your validation result and use FieldSet with FieldLegend for related controls.
accessibility: FieldControl supplies the control ID, described-by connection, and invalid state when used with the field parts.
Use either FieldDescription or FieldError for the shared message slot, or assign distinct IDs and an explicit aria-describedby when both are present.

hover-card.description: Shows supplementary preview content when a user hovers over or focuses its trigger.
usage: Use HoverCardTrigger for a link or focusable target and HoverCardContent for a brief preview.
Keep the destination and essential information available in the main interface.
accessibility: Treat hover-card content as supplementary; use a Popover or Dialog when users must interact with or reliably access the content.

icon.description: Renders named SVG icons and provides supporting icon-button and decorative disk primitives.
usage: Browse and search the icon pack in the live example. AnimatedIcon adds configurable motion; StateChevron follows open and closed trigger state.
Choose a supported icon name and size, then pair it with text to reinforce an action or status.
Use IconButton for an icon-only action and Disk when the icon needs a containing surface.
Friendly action aliases include check-circle, close, alert, loader, refresh and trash.
Default feedback responds once to the nearest enabled control with action-specific SVG-part motion. Set feedback={false} to opt out; draw mode owns its own animation.

The iconActionNames and iconActionDescriptions exports describe all 100 semantic actions. The searchable example pages through the complete family; new geometry retains Lucide and Feather license notices.
accessibility: Icons are hidden from assistive technology by default; give an IconButton its own accessible action name.

input.description: Collects a single-line value through a native input with optional composed affixes and clearing controls.
usage: Pass native type, name, value, and onChange props to match the data you need.
Use InputWrapper and InputControl for addons, and connect InputClear onClear to the input value.
accessibility: Associate a visible label with the input and connect instructions or errors using aria-describedby.
Use the native required and disabled attributes for those behaviors; visual variants alone do not enforce validation.

input-group.description: Combines a text control with adjacent prefixes, suffixes, or actions in one input surface.
usage: Place InputGroupInput or InputGroupTextarea with addons and text to show units or contextual information.
Use InputGroupButton for a related action and connect it to the same value through your state.
accessibility: Label the actual input or textarea and give each addon button an accessible name.
Associate meaningful prefixes, units, and instructions with the control instead of relying on visual adjacency alone.

input-otp.description: Presents a single code input as a sequence of visible character slots.
usage: Set maxLength and render a matching set of InputOTPSlot indexes inside InputOTPGroup.
Use value and onChange to capture the code and validate or submit it in your application.
accessibility: Label the underlying input, explain the expected code format, and associate any validation message with it.

item.description: Presents a compact content row with a title, supporting description, and optional trailing metadata.
usage: Compose ItemContent, ItemTitle, ItemDescription, and ItemTrailing for a readable list row.
Use the default button element for an action or choose an appropriate element through as for other content.
accessibility: Keep each actionable row clearly named and avoid nesting interactive controls inside the default button.
Expose any selection meaning with appropriate semantics in addition to the selected visual variant.

kbd.description: Formats a key or key combination as a recognizable keyboard instruction.
usage: Place key names inside Kbd next to the action they describe.
Use multiple key labels with readable separators when explaining a combination.
accessibility: Write understandable key names and surrounding instructions; displaying a shortcut does not install its keyboard handler.

label.description: Provides a native form label plus compact stat-label primitives for named values.
usage: Set htmlFor to the ID of a form control so the label identifies and activates it.
Use Stats and Stat to lay out concise named values when no form control is involved.
accessibility: Keep the label visible and specific; if using as to change the element, preserve the control association through appropriate semantics.

marker.description: Separates or annotates a sequence with a short event, status, or time label.
usage: Place a Marker between conversation or activity items to identify a date or milestone.
Use a status variant to reinforce an outcome that is also stated in the marker text.
accessibility: Keep the marker text meaningful in reading order; its visual treatment does not add a live-region announcement.

menubar.description: Groups application commands into a horizontal row of keyboard-navigable menus.
usage: Items show stable, varied blob adornments by default. Set adornment={false} to hide, supply {shape,color,icon,effect}, or pass a custom icon element.
Create one MenubarMenu per command family and connect each item to its action.
Use checkbox or radio items for persistent command settings and submenus for another level.
accessibility: Keep the menubar trigger and item primitives intact for their menu keyboard behavior.
Give triggers concise category names and implement any shortcuts shown by MenubarShortcut.

message.description: Structures a conversational or activity entry with a main content area and supporting description.
usage: Compose MessageContent and MessageDescription around the entry body and its context.
Combine with Avatar, Attachment, or Bubble when the entry needs an identity, file, or speech-style surface.
accessibility: Include sender, time, and status information in text where needed and preserve the intended message reading order.

message-scroller.description: Keeps a conversation near its latest content while allowing readers to scroll back without being pulled down.
usage: Place messages inside MessageScroller and add MessageScrollerJump to offer a return to the latest content.
Use followThreshold and onAtBottomChange to coordinate a nearby new-message indicator.
accessibility: Choose a suitable accessible label and announcement strategy for the conversation; the scroller does not create a live region automatically.
Provide a keyboard-reachable scrolling region when its content has no focusable elements.

native-select.description: Uses the browser’s native select control to choose from a compact list of options.
usage: Pass native name, value, and onChange props and compose NativeSelectOption children.
Use NativeSelectOptGroup to label related choices and disabled options for unavailable selections.
accessibility: Associate the select with a visible label and retain clear option text for the browser’s keyboard and assistive-technology behavior.

navigation-menu.description: Organizes destination links and optional expandable navigation panels.
usage: Items show stable, varied blob adornments by default. Set adornment={false} to hide, supply {shape,color,icon,effect}, or pass a custom icon element.
Use NavigationMenuLink for destinations and set active for the current page.
Compose triggers, content, and a viewport when a destination group needs an expandable panel.
accessibility: Give the navigation a useful label and use actual links for destinations.
Keep current-page state and the supplied trigger behavior when composing custom link content.

pagination.description: Lets users move between numbered pages and see their current position.
usage: Provide totalPages and handle onPageChange to update the displayed records.
Use page for controlled navigation or compose the pagination parts when you need a custom arrangement.
accessibility: The built-in controls identify the current page and announce the page count; preserve equivalent names and state in custom compositions.

popover.description: Places a dismissible panel next to a trigger for a small contextual task or set of controls.
usage: Compose PopoverTrigger and PopoverContent inside one root and add PopoverClose when an explicit close action helps.
Use controlled open state when the panel must follow another interaction.
accessibility: Give the trigger and panel clear accessible names and preserve focus and dismissal handling when customizing content.

preview.description: Pairs a live component example with a code view and a copy action.
usage: Pass the rendered example as children and its source as code.
Add a title and description that explain the example and the behavior to try.
accessibility: The view switch uses tabs and the copy result is announced; keep those controls and status available when extending the preview.

progress.description: Displays a measured amount of completion or an explicitly unavailable value.
usage: Set value and max for known progress, including zero as a valid measurement.
Use an unavailable value when completion cannot be measured and provide nearby context explaining why.
accessibility: Give the progressbar an accessible name through aria-label or aria-labelledby; the component exposes the numeric range or unavailable state.

questionnaire.description: Composes labeled questions, single-choice answers, and visible completion progress.
usage: The default organic selector stays close to a circle, with subtle asymmetry and cursor-responsive contour motion.
Choose organic, circle, rounded, pebble, leaf or flower; pink, blue, olive and yellow tones are available.
Group each question in QuestionnaireQuestion and place value-based QuestionnaireOption parts inside QuestionnaireOptions.
Store answers through onValueChange and update QuestionnaireProgress from your own completion logic.
selectorSize, selectorIndicator and showSelectorIndicator configure the selection mark; labels retain a minimum44px row target.
accessibility: Use a legend for each fieldset and label its radio group with aria-labelledby or aria-label.
Keep option labels descriptive and pass required or descriptive attributes through inputProps when needed.

radio-group.description: Lets users select one option from a labeled set of mutually exclusive choices.
usage: The default organic selector stays close to a circle, with subtle asymmetry and cursor-responsive contour motion.
Choose organic, circle, rounded, pebble, leaf or flower; pink, blue, olive and yellow tones are available.
Give each RadioGroupItem a distinct value and use value or defaultValue on the root.
Handle onValueChange to update the setting or form answer represented by the group.
Use size="sm" | "default" | "lg" or a numeric16–64px size. indicator chooses auto/dot/check/diamond/flower; showIndicator={false} leaves the selected outer blob only.
accessibility: Name the group and associate each item with a visible label; preserve the supplied radio parts for keyboard navigation and checked state.

Arrow and Home/End navigation preserve Radix focus management and activate the focused radio even for immediate keydown/keyup pairs. Tab navigation does not change selection; disabled options are skipped.

resizable.description: Divides a region into panels whose relative sizes can be adjusted with a separator.
usage: Compose ResizablePanel elements and ResizableHandle inside ResizablePanelGroup.
Choose horizontal or vertical direction and set panel size limits to keep each pane usable.
accessibility: Preserve the separator primitive for keyboard resizing and give the panels meaningful content headings or labels.

scroll-area.description: Contains overflowing content in a bounded viewport with styled scrollbars.
usage: Set a height or width constraint so the viewport can scroll within its surrounding layout.
Add a horizontal ScrollBar when wide content needs horizontal scrolling.
accessibility: Keep scrolling content keyboard-reachable and give an independently scrollable region a useful name when it needs one.

select.description: Opens a list of options from a trigger and stores one selected value.
usage: Items show stable, varied blob adornments by default. Set adornment={false} to hide, supply {shape,color,icon,effect}, or pass a custom icon element.
Compose SelectTrigger, SelectValue, SelectContent, and value-based SelectItem parts.
Use value and onValueChange for controlled state, and groups or labels to organize a longer list.
SelectItem shows a persistent selected check separately from hover or keyboard emphasis. Set showIndicator=false to suppress that mark.
accessibility: Associate a visible label with the trigger and retain the supplied item parts for keyboard navigation and selection announcements.

separator.description: Divides adjacent content with a horizontal or vertical rule.
usage: Use a separator between sections that need a visible boundary.
Set orientation for the layout and decorative when the line carries no structural meaning.
accessibility: Set decorative for purely visual rules to remove separator semantics; meaningful separators expose their orientation.

shape.description: A shared catalogue of 36 SVG silhouettes, with 12 original contours that morph smoothly between shapes.
usage: Use Shape with a name from shapeNames for a static mask. Size it through className or style and set its fill with the --c custom property.
Use ShapeMorph with a name from signatureShapeNames for an animated contour. Change name to morph from the visible shape; choose fill or outline and set color through ordinary SVG styles.
Use the shared silhouettes for card accents, empty states and dividers. Motion Off, reduced motion and offscreen rendering settle to a static shape.
accessibility: Shapes are decorative by default. Give ShapeMorph a label only when the graphic conveys meaning; keep descriptive text beside decorative accents.

sheet.description: Opens a side surface for focused secondary content while the current page remains in place.
usage: Compose SheetTrigger, SheetContent, title, description, and close parts for a secondary workflow.
Use open and onOpenChange to coordinate the sheet with application state.

SheetContent side="start" or side="end" (default) follows reading direction. Explicit dir overrides a surrounding Radix DirectionProvider. The panel travels its full measured distance to the viewport edge.
accessibility: Include SheetTitle and a clear close action and retain the dialog primitives for focus management and dismissal.

sidebar.description: Provides a collapsible navigation rail with grouped destinations, active states, and a footer area.
usage: Compose SidebarHeader, SidebarContent, menu buttons, and SidebarFooter around your destination links.
Use SidebarProvider for shared open state and choose container or viewport layout for its placement.
accessibility: Provide a label for icon-only destinations and set isActive on the current link.
Preserve the trigger’s expanded state and the navigation label when composing custom content.

skeleton.description: Reserves the visual shape of content while its real data is still loading.
usage: Choose skeleton shapes and groups that approximate the content that will replace them.
Replace placeholders with the completed content or a useful error state when loading finishes.
AsyncContent accepts optional loading and fallback props. The real content stays mounted across loading changes so input edits survive; omitted loading preserves the original static wrapper.
accessibility: Hide decorative placeholders from assistive technology and expose the loading state once on the surrounding content region.

slider.description: Adjusts one or more numeric values by moving labeled thumbs along a track.
usage: Set min, max, and step for the value domain and use value or defaultValue arrays for the thumbs.
Use SliderOutput or nearby text to show the current value and its unit.
accessibility: Provide thumbLabel for every thumb, using the index callback when their meanings differ.
Keep the numeric value understandable without relying on the thumb position alone.

spinner.description: Shows that work is in progress when an exact completion amount is unavailable.
usage: Set label to describe the work, such as loading a preview or saving changes.
Use Progress instead when a meaningful completion value is available.
accessibility: The spinner supplies a status role and a working label; avoid duplicate announcements when a surrounding control already describes the same busy state.

stepper.description: Tracks the current stage of a multi-step sequence and provides previous and next controls.
usage: Set count and optional labels, then use one-based values for StepperItem parts.
Use onValueChange to switch your content and gate progression with your own validation before advancing.
StepperList orientation="horizontal" lays out connected milestones with native Previous/Next controls. The default remains vertical. Completed milestones use a native validation icon.
accessibility: The current item exposes aria-current="step"; use meaningful titles and include StepperStatus when a spoken progress update is useful.

switch.description: Turns a named binary setting on or off.
usage: Use checked and onCheckedChange when the setting is stored in application state.
Pair the control with a label, or use SwitchRow to arrange it with explanatory text.
accessibility: Keep the setting name stable as the state changes and associate it with the switch; the checked state communicates whether it is on.

table.description: Presents structured data in native rows and columns with headers and an optional caption.
usage: Compose TableHeader, TableBody, TableRow, TableHead, and TableCell for the data structure.
Use TableContainer for overflow and numeric cells for aligned values; add TableCaption to explain the table.
accessibility: Use real header cells and appropriate scope attributes so row and column relationships are clear.

tabs.description: Switches between related content panels while keeping the available views visible.
usage: Match each TabsTrigger value to a TabsContent value inside a shared Tabs root.
Use value and onValueChange when another control needs to select a view, and choose a variant for its visual hierarchy.
Panel changes use the shared presence transition. Exiting panels become inert and leave after their exit; forceMount opts into consumer-managed visibility.
accessibility: Give TabsList a descriptive accessible name and preserve the supplied trigger and panel relationships for keyboard navigation.

textarea.description: Collects multiline text and offers composer and character-count parts for longer input.
usage: Pass native rows, value, and onChange props for notes, descriptions, or message drafts.
Use TextareaCount with the same value for a count display and set maxLength on the textarea when a limit must be enforced.
accessibility: Associate a visible label and instructions with the textarea and connect validation errors through aria-describedby.

toast.description: Reports a brief outcome in a notification area without moving the user away from the current task.
usage: Place ToastProvider and ToastViewport around controlled Toast instances with a title or description.
Use durable for a message that should not time out and provide a close action; use ToastAction for a relevant optional follow-up.
accessibility: Provide ToastAction altText that explains the action’s purpose and keep a reachable dismissal control.
Keep critical instructions available outside a timed toast when users need time to act on them.

toggle.description: Represents an action or option that stays pressed until it is toggled again.
usage: Use pressed and onPressedChange for controlled state or defaultPressed for a local default.
Use a stable action label for formatting or view options that can be enabled independently.
accessibility: Keep the accessible name stable so aria-pressed communicates the changing state; name icon-only toggles explicitly.

toggle-group.description: Groups pressable choices that can allow one or several selected values.
usage: Set type="single" for one selected value or type="multiple" for an array of choices.
Give each ToggleGroupItem a distinct value and handle onValueChange to apply the selection.
accessibility: Name the group and every item, especially when choices use icons, and preserve the supplied pressed states and keyboard behavior.

tooltip.description: Adds a short supplementary explanation to a trigger on hover or keyboard focus.
usage: Compose TooltipTrigger and TooltipContent inside Tooltip and use TooltipProvider to share timing settings.
Use the tooltip for concise clarification, such as explaining a labeled icon action.
accessibility: Give the trigger its own accessible name and keep essential instructions available without the tooltip.
Use a Popover for interactive content instead of placing controls inside a tooltip.

typography.description: Provides text roles for headings, body copy, metadata, values, and identifiers.
usage: Choose a role such as Hero, SectionTitle, Body, Meta, or Identifier to establish a readable hierarchy.
Use as to select the semantic element while retaining the intended text treatment.
accessibility: Choose heading levels from the document structure and use paragraphs, labels, and code elements according to their meaning.

animated-number.description: A smooth, interruptible number transition for totals, metrics and small moments of progress.
usage: Pass a numeric value; updates animate from the current displayed value. The initial render shows the actual total. Non-finite values show the fallback (an em dash by default), never a fabricated zero.
Use locale and format for currency, percentages or compact notation. Reserve enough width for the largest expected value.
Use an external live status only when the update needs announcing.
accessibility: Assistive technology receives the final formatted value without every intermediate animation frame.
Reduced motion, global Off and offscreen updates settle immediately.

text-reveal.description: Readable word, grapheme, phrase or measured-line arrivals with soft focus, fold and organic scale choices.
usage: Choose rise, fade, soften, fold, bloom, scale or settle. Bloom includes a small overshoot; scale gently grows; settle moves a slightly enlarged phrase into place.

Choose split="word", "grapheme", "text" or "line". Line mode measures real browser wrapping, including hard breaks, and remeasures after resizing or font loading. It renders a block; use it for headings and short passages.
Change replayKey to replay deliberately. Duration is bounded to 0–1500ms and the total stagger delay is distributed evenly within 600ms, including long text.
Text Reveal is an entrance effect and stays readable after playback or interruption. Use the Presence components when content also needs an exit lifecycle.

Line mode measures up to 4000 graphemes. Longer prose stays fully readable in its normal layout without line animation. Resizing settles the text rather than replaying it; replayKey starts a new arrival.
accessibility: The complete text is exposed once; animated visual fragments are hidden from assistive technology.
Reduced motion, Motion Off and Flow Off show the still state. Leaving the viewport during playback settles text; returning does not replay the same content.
Use word, whole-phrase or measured-line grouping for scripts whose letters join across grapheme boundaries.

shape-scene.description: A tactile 3D composition made from Cojeev shapes, with a static fallback and motion preferences built in.
usage: Place the sculpture beside generous typography. Its reserved aspect ratio keeps the surrounding layout stable while it loads.
Choose from sixteen authored shapes and clay, glazed, grain or ripple shader materials. The default palette follows AppearanceProvider; explicit warm/cool palettes are also available.
This optional entry installs Three.js; the rest of the library does not require it. Initialization waits until the scene enters the viewport.
Procedural object-space grain and flowing contour shaders use the existing lighting pass. Offscreen and hidden scenes pause; palette changes recolour meshes without rebuilding the context.
accessibility: Provide a useful aria-label when the artwork conveys meaning, or aria-hidden for a decorative composition.
Global Off and reduced motion stop ambient and pointer motion. Offscreen and hidden scenes pause work.
Without WebGL2 the authored static shapes remain visible, with a clear fallback description.

multi-select.description: Searchable multiple choices with removable selections, form values and clear validation.
usage: Items show stable, varied blob adornments by default. Set adornment={false} to hide, supply {shape,color,icon,effect}, or pass a custom icon element.
Use value and onValueChange for controlled selection, or defaultValue for internal state. A name submits repeated values with a native form.
Disabled options stay locked. Values no longer present in options stay visible and removable, so filtering does not silently discard a selection.
Use description for guidance and error for validation. This component handles a bounded local set of choices; it does not fetch or virtualize options.
accessibility: The trigger has a visible label. Search, independently checked options and removable tokens expose their own accessible names.
Arrow keys, Home and End move through enabled choices; Space toggles. Escape closes the popup and returns focus.
A disabled field closes and locks its controls. Error text is announced and linked to the invalid trigger.

ambient-background.description: Adds a quiet animated composition around content, with decorative shapes kept behind a readable surface.
usage: Choose drift, orbit, or contour for a welcome section, introduction, or decorative pause between sections.
Pass children for foreground content and control paused when the surrounding experience should stop the decoration.
accessibility: Decoration is hidden and inert; foreground children keep their own semantics.
Global motion Off and reduced-motion preferences produce a static composition; offscreen or hidden content pauses its animation.

marquee.description: A measured moving list with optional perspective and a rhythm that follows scrolling.
usage: Use decorative text, shapes or non-interactive cards as children. The list is measured after fonts, content and viewport changes; its visual copy has no duplicate IDs or mounted React effects.
Choose a named speed or set pixelsPerSecond (0–160). direction is left or right. Changes of pace and scroll direction preserve the current position.
presentation=depth adds bounded perspective and distance-based focus. Adjust tiltX, tiltY, perspective and depth. Quiet settings restore flat, fully legible content.
respondToScroll follows the document by default. Pass scrollTarget to follow a mounted native scroll viewport instead. Pair two rows with opposite direction values for a counter-moving composition.
Pause keeps the current position. Hover and focus pause automatic motion. Children with real links, buttons or fields are displayed as a static original list so all actions remain usable.
accessibility: One semantic list is exposed to assistive technology. Its decorative copy is inert and hidden.
Reduced motion, local and shared quiet preferences disable movement. Hidden and offscreen rows stop work. Automatic motion has an explicit pause control.
Use normal typography for important reading. Depth and outlined text are expressive options for short, non-essential phrases.

agent-state.description: A sculpted, living status field that changes contour and color as an agent thinks, works, asks for input, or finishes.
usage: Use status to convey actual activity: idle, thinking, working, needs-input, complete or error.
Use sm beside a task, md in a conversation, and lg for a focused empty or waiting state.
The field pauses outside the viewport, when the document is hidden, and when motion is disabled.
accessibility: Visible labels accompany color and shape; provide a precise label for your workflow.
Status is announced politely. Use one live state indicator per active task to avoid duplicate announcements.
Reduced motion preserves the status contour without continuous animation.

agent-chat.description: A composable agent conversation with a bounded thread, draft composer, attachments, progress, explicit permissions and choice prompts.
usage: Compose AgentChatHeader, AgentChatThread and AgentChatComposer inside AgentChat.
Keep messages, draft, selected files and request status in your application. Clear a draft only after onSend accepts it.
Use AgentChatPermission for deliberate allow/deny decisions. Render its receipt after a decision.
Use AgentChatOptions to collect one valid choice; Continue remains disabled until a valid enabled option is selected.
The documentation runs a local simulation. Connect callbacks to your own application to perform real work.
accessibility: The thread is a keyboard-reachable live log and follows only while the reader stays near its end.
Enter inserts a new line. Command/Ctrl+Enter sends. Stop preserves the conversation.
Label attachments and permission scope clearly. Do not treat a preset option as submitted consent.
Return focus to the next useful control after a request resolves or is cancelled.

theme-toggle.description: A controlled light/dark switch with a morphing sun and moon and a smooth organic page reveal.
usage: The destination theme opens through a slower organic reveal with a varied viewport origin. Explicit origin options remain available; reduced motion and Motion Off settle immediately.
Pass mode and onModeChange. Keep persistence in the application.
Call applyTheme(nextMode, quiet) to animate the document theme, or update your own theme scope.
Use the shared motion preference so reduced motion and Motion Off switch immediately.
accessibility: The button exposes a named switch and aria-checked.
Both keyboard Space and Enter change the controlled mode.

animated-icon.description: Contextual motion for the shared icon catalog: draw, tremor, spinning settings, bouncing navigation and morphing validation.
usage: Use inside a named Button or link. Hover and focus are inherited from that control.
Set active for a processing state; omit it for pointer and focus interaction.
Choose a preset to override the name-based default.
The auto preset chooses action-specific SVG-part feedback. Explicit presets keep their own visual treatment, and bounce follows the icon direction.
Use active to control feedback directly. amplitude={0} suppresses movement. Loader auto feedback repeats only while active; other action reactions are finite.
Auto maps all 100 semantic action names to original part-level feedback. Only loader loops while active; finite feedback settles for other actions. Search by name or action in the example.
accessibility: Icons remain decorative beside a text label.
Motion pauses offscreen, while the document is hidden, and when reduced motion or Motion Off is enabled.

presence.description: MotionPresence keeps keyed children mounted for their exits. MotionSurface adds coordinated lifecycle states to an existing primitive.
usage: Keep the MotionPresence boundary mounted and give changing children stable keys.
Use MotionSurface asChild around exactly one ref-capable primitive.
Use quiet motion to settle immediately; the shared preference is inherited.
Use settle for a small scale-down exit, soften for upward blurred words, or focus for whole-phrase focus changes. These use a gentle 420ms default exit; existing presets keep their earlier timings.

Set exitDelay on sibling words for a departure sequence; it is capped at 600ms. exitDuration is seconds, bounded to 0–2. The caller controls removal, rather than a video timeline disappearing live content.

For staggered words, a keyed conditional heading inside MotionPresence may contain MotionSurface asChild spans. Keep a single accessible heading label and hide the animated fragments. Soft-focus presets own CSS filter; use a separate wrapper if the child already has an authored filter.

Directional blur can be composed with MotionSurface preset="soften": provide signed x or y and a blur in initial/exit, then zero x/y and blur in animate. Keep it inside MotionPresence for real removal; no separate wrapper primitive is needed.
accessibility: Preserve native semantics with asChild.
Put presence outside the actual conditional removal; an inner boundary cannot retain its own parent.
Exiting surfaces are inert and hidden from assistive technology until removed; quiet preferences remove the delay and motion.

appearance.description: Choose from six coordinated palettes and adjust reading contrast across the application.
usage: Mount AppearanceProvider once around your application. AppearanceMenu or AppearanceControls changes the shared appearance.
Palettes and contrast persist in local storage. Controlled value/onValueChange is available for your own settings surface.
Contrast adjusts semantic text and edges; it does not filter artwork or alter accent fills.
accessibility: Text role pairs retain at least 4.5:1 on primary surfaces at every setting. Control edges retain 3:1.

scroll-organism.description: A softly stretching companion driven by native document scrolling.
usage: Position the decorative organism at the edge of a scrolling story. Tune shape, size and travel.
It uses Motion values without per-frame React renders or scroll interception.
accessibility: The decorative organism is hidden from assistive technology and ignores pointer events.

assembly-part.description: A persistent native component moving between a floating organism and its measured layout.
usage: Use this primitive inside a measured composition. Preserve stable part identity while target geometry changes.
asChild retains the native interactive element. Assembly controls manage its interactivity during travel.
accessibility: Settled parts retain native keyboard behaviour. Moving parts are inert until placed.

Focus uses a real local elapsed-time countdown. Invite records local RSVP state; provide callbacks for your application.
accessibility: Moving controls remain inert until arrival, then regain normal keyboard, hover and form behavior.

organism-assembly.description: An interactive studio that gathers floating shapes into six reusable compositions.
usage: Choose Profile, Panel, Dock, Chat, Focus or Invite. Replay scatters and reassembles their native parts.

accessibility: Arrow keys, Home and End navigate the chooser; the mobile grid keeps all six choices visible.
Motion Off and reduced motion keep controls immediately usable and disable replay.

focus-session.description: A local focus timer composed from Cojeev cards, progress, badges and native controls.
usage: Import FocusSession from the focus-session entry. Set durationSeconds (default 1500, bounded to 1–86400) and optional name or description.

Use onAction for start, pause, reset and complete events. OrganismProps also supports controlled state/onStateChange and assembly presentation.
The documentation timer is a local demo. It does not create a reminder, notification or saved task, and reloading clears its state.
accessibility: Native buttons support keyboard activation. Remaining time and progress stay available as readable values.
Reduced motion and global Off preserve the usable timer; decorative motion is independent of elapsed time.

invite-card.description: An event invitation with participant avatars and a reversible local RSVP, composed from Cojeev primitives.
usage: Import InviteCard from the invite-card entry. Set name, description, inviteDate, inviteTime and inviteLocation to describe the event.
Pass up to four participants as {name, initials}. The yes/no controls update the local rsvp state and emit onAction with action='rsvp' and value='yes' or 'no'.
Use controlled state/onStateChange when the response belongs to your application. Persistence and delivery remain the consumer's responsibility.
The documentation example is a fictional invitation. Its responses stay in the preview and send no invitation, email or calendar update.
accessibility: Event details are text; native RSVP buttons remain keyboard accessible and expose their current selection.
The quiet-motion settings preserve assembled, usable controls and readable invitation details.

accessibility: Keyboard focus gives the same arrow feedback as hover.
Motion Off, Flow Off and reduced motion keep a static arrow and usable control.

depth-background.description: Layered pollen, contours and orbital shapes with perspective, native-scroll depth and pointer response.
usage: Place inside a positioned section; the background fills its parent without intercepting clicks.
Choose a variant and stable seed. Tune density from 0.35 to 2 and intensity from 0 to 2; zero intensity keeps it still.
accessibility: Decorative, hidden from assistive technology and never focusable.
Offscreen, hidden-page and reduced-motion states stop its movement. Keep text on a readable foreground.

float-layer.description: An entrance, scroll depth and gentle idle movement for a real component or a group of elements.
usage: Set depth and drift in pixels. Use depth={0} drift={0} for a stationary foreground after its entrance; reserve idle drift and parallax for background layers.
Tune revealDuration (0.2–2 seconds), revealDistance (0–80 pixels) and delay. Set replay to reveal again whenever the layer re-enters the viewport.
The default wrapper keeps transforms separate. asChild preserves the child element; use the wrapper when that child owns an inline CSS translate.
accessibility: Server-rendered content stays readable before hydration.
Reduced motion and Motion Off leave content visible and still; offscreen and hidden-page work pauses.

shape-artwork.description: An original SVG silhouette with a cast shadow and a rotated rear outline. The same vector layers power its live preview and standalone SVG export.
usage: Set name to one of the 12 signature shapes; choose pink, olive, blue or yellow with tone. Set rotation in degrees and filled={false} for an outlined foreground.
Use shadow and echo to toggle the cast shadow and rear outline. shadowAngle sets the cast direction clockwise from the right; echoAngle rotates the rear outline relative to the foreground.

shapeArtworkSvg(options, colors?) returns an original standalone SVG string; supply resolved fill, shadow and echo colors to preserve a customized palette. Its fixed viewBox contains every supported shape at all layer angles.

shapeArtworkCode(options) returns a React usage snippet containing every selected prop. The landing workbench downloads a transparent SVG and provides accessible copying with visible success or failure feedback.
Live name changes morph through the shared choreography policy. Rotation and layer changes follow the supplied props; no idle foreground motion is added.
accessibility: The SVG is decorative by default. Supply label when the graphic conveys meaning; native SVG props and refs are forwarded.
Motion Off, Flow Off, reduced motion and hidden or offscreen rendering settle the contour immediately.
The example changes local artwork settings only. Export is vector artwork, with the selected target contour rather than a transient animation frame.

word-relay.description: Exchanges phrases, words or letters inside a stable wrapping footprint, with interruptible motion and explicit navigation.
usage: Pass words and optionally control index/onIndexChange. All candidates share one wrapping layout footprint, so the surrounding content stays in place.

Choose split="phrase" (default), "word" or "grapheme". staggerFrom="first", "last", "center" or "edges" sets the logical arrival order; direction="up" or "down" sets travel. Stagger is milliseconds, evenly bounded to a 500ms window.

Automatic changes are opt-in through auto; pair with a pause control. interval is 1200–60000ms and always allows the transition plus at least 500ms at rest. duration is 0–1600ms. loop=false stops at the last phrase.

Use controlsRef for next(), previous(), jumpTo(index) and reset(). The normal ref still returns the span. Controlled navigation requests onIndexChange; the parent must apply the new index. reset returns to defaultIndex.
Use tone="inherit" inside a heading, or a native accent tone for an organic highlight.
accessibility: Only the current phrase is exposed to assistive technology; animated layers are hidden. Add aria-live only if the content warrants announcements.
Hover and focus pause automatic playback. Reduced motion, shared Motion Off, Flow Off, hidden tabs and offscreen content suspend the timer.
Empty words produce an empty span, and out-of-range indexes clamp to the available phrases.
Grapheme grouping preserves emoji and combining marks; use word or phrase grouping to preserve joining in scripts such as Arabic.

reading-trail.description: Tracks actual reading progress and links to named sections with a quiet organic marker.
usage: Pass items with existing document IDs and readable labels. Native anchors remain available before JavaScript.
Use scrollRoot for a contained scrolling panel. The default tracks the document; offset sets the current-section activation line.
Duplicate IDs are consolidated. Missing sections do not claim measured progress.
accessibility: Links preserve modifier clicks and normal URLs. A selected destination receives focus.
Current section is exposed through aria-current. Optional smooth scrolling respects shared quiet settings.

living-link.description: A native link with a drawn ink contour, directional underline reveals, or an organic pigment wash.
usage: Pass href and normal anchor attributes. direction can be forward or up-right.
Use disabled to keep an announced, unavailable label without a navigable URL.
treatment selects contour (the original resting mark), underline-start, underline-end, underline-center, wash-up or wash-across. Start/end follow the reading direction.
tone selects pink, olive, blue or yellow for a restrained wash; text keeps its theme ink throughout the transition. Arrows exchange through a small window in the five new treatments.
accessibility: Native link navigation, modifier clicks and keyboard activation remain intact.
Hover and focus share the same emphasis. Disabled anchors leave the tab order. Reduced motion keeps a still, readable underline.

pigment-field.description: An original GPU pigment wash using the current Cojeev palette.
usage: Place inside a positioned parent with a height. Keep meaningful content in a sibling above the decorative field.
Control tone, speed (0–3), intensity (0–2) and paused. The canvas caps pixel density and responds to resizing.
This background is an original shader foundation; it does not yet implement pointer-fluid refraction over HTML.
Place text on an opaque native Card or other readable surface over the changing artwork; do not assume contrast against every shader pixel.
accessibility: Decorative canvas is inert, hidden from assistive technology and never captures pointer events.
Reduced motion, offscreen content, document visibility and shared Motion/Flow Off suspend continuous rendering. A static fallback covers unavailable or lost contexts.

contour-field.description: Original topographic lines on the inherited paper surface, with a bounded GPU renderer.
usage: Place inside a positioned parent with a height. Keep content outside the decorative field.
Control tone, speed (0–3), intensity (0–2) and paused. A still fallback is available when GPU rendering cannot run.
Use an opaque native surface for meaningful text placed above the changing artwork.
accessibility: The field is decorative, inert and ignores pointer hit testing.
Animation suspends with reduced motion, shared quiet settings, hidden tabs and offscreen content.

milestone-path.description: A readable sequence of milestones with supplied status, details and optional actions.
usage: Pass stable IDs and explicit complete, current or upcoming states. Supply title, description and metadata for context.
Provide onMilestoneSelect only when a milestone has a real action. Noninteractive milestones remain ordinary content.
MilestonePath composes the existing Stepper parts. The caller owns explicit states; it does not invent a separate selected-row model.
accessibility: Progress state is named in text as well as color. Buttons retain native keyboard and disabled behavior.
The ordered sequence remains meaningful with motion disabled or without an interactive action.

activity-feed.description: Chronological activity composed from native avatars, badges, content rows and motion surfaces.
usage: Pass entries in the order they should appear, with stable IDs and optional actor, timestamp, badge and details.
Omit initialVisible to show all supplied entries. Set initialVisible and pageSize to reveal supplied history in pages.
The feed displays your data; it does not fetch, manufacture events or reorder timestamps.
accessibility: A semantic ordered list preserves chronology. Show more announces the new count and moves focus to the first newly shown entry.
Images are decorative alongside named actors. New content respects the shared reduced-motion contract.

text-ribbon.description: A measured phrase follows six original SVG paths, with direct manipulation and gentle changes of pace.
usage: Choose circle, loop, wave, arch, line or figure-eight. Circle has a compact square artwork; the other paths scale from a 640 × 280 viewBox.
Automatic motion is opt-in with auto. Supply a visible pause control via paused. Speed is bounded to 0–120 SVG units per second; fontSize is bounded to 24–56.
Use a short decorative phrase. The visual path repeats it, while assistive technology reads the text once. Use guide and tone to show a simple path or a native accent stroke.
Set curvature from 0 to 1 for the arch and wave. Choose hoverBehavior=pause, slow, quicken or none; pace changes ease continuously.
draggable adds direct horizontal manipulation, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and Home. Vertical touch gestures preserve scrolling. Automatic movement is still opt-in.
Omit direction for local direction after a drag, or supply direction/onDirectionChange to own it. Paused and quiet settings stop automatic travel while explicit positioning remains available.
accessibility: Keep critical prose in ordinary readable text. A curved ribbon works best as an optional expressive detail.

Focus pauses movement. Hover pauses by default; slow and quicken are optional. Reduced motion, local data-flow=off, data-no-glide, shared Motion Off, Flow Off, hidden documents and offscreen views suspend automatic travel.
The SVG is hidden from assistive technology. The complete supplied phrase remains in the accessible DOM, including when motion is disabled.

A static fallback remains when Canvas2D is unavailable. Failed local imports report an actionable message and retain the previous sculpture.

semantic-bloom.description: A living wordmark whose particles wander, connect and gather into a liquid organism. Adapted from ThreeUI with Cojeev colors and motion controls.
usage: Use text for a readable DOM wordmark. Choose tone="signature", "memory", "together" or "ink"; colors follow the surrounding design tokens. The host has a default minimum height and accepts className/style.

Tune physics: particleCount (8–100), radius (6–28), speed (0–2), wander (0–1), damping (0.8–0.98), pointerAttraction (0–3), pointerRadius (0–600), textAttraction (0–3), textRadius (0–400), connectionDistance (0–240). Distances are CSS pixels. Invalid numeric values fall back to safe defaults.

Tune size (0.55–1.6), opacity (0–1, artwork only), softness (0–20), edgeTexture (0–40), and connectionWidth (0–8). Zero connection width removes links. Very small particles with a large blur can dissolve; reduce softness to expose individual particles.

Pass controlsRef for gather(), scatter() and reset(); connect these to native buttons or real application events. seed provides a repeatable initial arrangement. onWordActive reports decorative proximity only, not semantic analysis.

Source-based adaptation of ThreeUI Semantic Bloom (MIT, copyright 2026 Meng To). Original force defaults and liquid filter retained; native container coordinates, fixed 60Hz simulation, palette and lifecycle replace the iframe. See docs/semantic-bloom.md and reference/semantic-bloom for attribution and a runnable baseline.
accessibility: The complete wordmark is selectable, wrapping DOM text. The canvas/filter/fallback are decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Essential meaning must not depend on particles or onWordActive.
